newsitem.title: KENYA: ICRC leaves Zairean town, sounds alarm over aid.
newsitem.headline: ICRC leaves Zairean town, sounds alarm over aid.

text.p: The last two staff of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) pulled out of the Zairean town of Kindu for security reasons on Wednesday, saying thousands of people were without aid in the region.

An ICRC statement said the last international ICRC delegate and a Zairean ICRC worker left Kindu, 400 km (250 miles) south of northeastern regional centre Kisangani, temporarily for Kinshasa following another expatriate who was pulled out on Tuesday.
It said they left because of "precarious security" in Kindu, which rebels said on Wednesday they had seized, and to try to draw up a plan to aid all victims of conflict in the region.
Kindu residents said on Wednesday the town was still in government hands.
The ICRC said the health of Zairean displaced by fighting arriving in Kindu was extremely poor and it had been the only international aid agency working in the region for weeks.
A multinational force has been gathering in Uganda for the past two weeks but has so far been unable to bring any aid to Rwandan refugees and Zaireans in the east displaced by fighting since October.
The ICRC cited the case of a nine-year-old girl who arrived from the eastern town of Bukavu unable to speak and suffering from exhaustion, malaria, dehydration, malnutrition and shock.
It said she had wandered without help for 10 days.
"The ICRC (also) expresses the strongest concern about the dozens of thousands of civilians, displaced and refugees, without humanitarian aid for weeks in the region of Shabunda," it said.
Shabunda is 170 km (105 miles) east of Kindu and about halfway on the road from the eastern Zairean city of Bukavu, which was seized in October by Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels.
